en.html:
I remember.

What these two arms are guilty of, I remember.

The smell of blood, I remember.

The last breath, I remember.

Those eyes going empty, the light leaving them—I remember.

All those deaths. I remember them.

...Why did I kill those people?

My reason—

To the people I killed, to their loved ones left behind, what explanation can I give? From the beginning, none. I killed them by my own decision. In front of them, my reason has no weight. There is no escape for me from their hatred, from their condemnation.

To me only, the reason means something.

...I killed them.

So that even more people would not die.

So that the Silver Star's disaster would not multiply. The warrior who had received its egg, and the other person Muramasa's nature inevitably demanded—I chose them as sacrifices and cut off their heads.

If now I accept the Silver Star's existence, then what did I take their lives for?

For them, probably, being forced to die had no value at all.
And now even I, who forced it on them, will say those deaths had no value?

Then they—
Their deaths—

ja.html:
俺は覚えている。

　この両腕の罪を覚えている。

　血の匂いを覚えている。

　最後の吐息を覚えている。

　瞳が空虚に、輝きを失ってゆく様を覚えている。

　数多の死を覚えている。

　……何故、俺は彼らを殺したのか。

　その理由――

　殺した彼らに、彼らの残された近親者に、釈明する
言葉としてのそれは最初から無い。
　俺は己一個の意思決定で殺したのだから、その理由
に意味はなく、憎悪と断罪を免れる道は絶無である。

　殺害理由は、俺自身にのみ意味を持つ。

　……俺は。

　より多くの人を死なせないため、彼らを殺した。

　銀星号の災厄を増殖させまい、と。
〝卵〟を享けた武者と、村正の特質が必然として求む
もう一人の人間を、<ruby>犠牲<rt>サクリファイス</rt></ruby>に選んで首を刎ねた。

　俺がもし、今になって銀星号の存在を許容するなら
――彼らは一体何のために命を奪われたのか。

　彼らはおそらくその主観において、全く無価値な死
を遂げねばならなかった。
　それを強いた俺すらも、彼らの死の価値を否定する
のなら。

　彼らは、
　彼らの死は、――――――――

en.html:
When my awareness returned to the outside world, first came a terrible feeling of being out of place.
Time and space had lost the connection, you could say. Reality was in front of me, but recognizing it as reality—I couldn't.

Probably because the Silver Star's mental contamination had been lifted.
Everything inside my skull was rapidly being put back in order, back into its original shape. Having to go through that, it was like being forcibly made mad.

When my awareness returned to the outside world, first came a terrible feeling of being out of place.
Time and space had lost the connection, you could say. Reality was in front of me, but recognizing it as reality—I couldn't.

Probably because the Silver Star's mental contamination had been lifted.
Everything inside my skull was rapidly being put back in order, back into its original shape. Having to go through that, it was like being forcibly made mad.

en.html:
Muramasa held me up and pressed a hand to my forehead.
Such a cold hand. Was it always like that, or had she done something to it? I couldn't tell.

...What a relief.
This coldness was helping.

A warm hand would have felt pleasant.
Perhaps all the strength would have left me. Drowsiness, and then sleep.

But this cold hand gave me strength.
Enough to stand on my own two feet.

...Achha.

Steel. That was the coldness I was feeling.
Strength itself had this temperature.

en.html:
I—

...What else could I do? I waited.

Muramasa was sobbing with guilt and regret I could not understand. I held her up without saying anything.
Inside her, where there was supposed to be nothing but unshakable iron, a storm was raging. What wisdom did I have for that? None. I just kept waiting for it to pass.

に吹き荒れる嵐が去るのを、知恵も無く待ち続けた。
